newsitem.title: USA: Apache to supply Egyptian grid with gas.
newsitem.headline: Apache to supply Egyptian grid with gas.

text.p: Apache Corp said on Thursday it and its partners have agreed to supply 200 million cubic feet of gas per day from the Khalda Concession in western Egypt to Egypt's national grid system under a 25-year take-or-pay contract beginning May 1, 1999.

The contract price -- now more than $3 per thousand cubic feet at the wellhead -- is tied to the price of fuel oil and Gulf of Suez blended crude oil, Apache said. At current prices, Apache said its share of future deliveries represented about $1.2 billion, 75 percent of which was contracted under take-or-pay provisions.
Net reserves from Apache's contractor interest over the life of the contract amount to about 400 billion cubic feet equivalent, the company said.
For 1996, Apache said it expected to book reserves of about 85 Bcf of gas equivalent from discoveries made to date on the concession.
Apache and its partners in the Khalda Concession of Egypt's Western Desert have delivery capacity exceeding 200 MMcf per day, the company said.
Independent proved reserve estimates for existing Khalda fields are about 320 Bcf of gas equivalent, it said.
Active exploration and development continues on the concession, Apache said.
